summary: What worked: halving TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^18 while keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 128 (grad_accum 2->1) took val_bpb from 0.997333 to 0.987686 at identical token throughput -- the gain is purely more optimizer steps. Adding more model capacity on top (depth 10 at d512) gave my best, 0.985236. What did not work: going further down to 2^17 or to DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 gives back the whole gain, because halving device batch costs ~15% of tokens to fixed per-step overhead; scaling all four LRs by 1.4x was worse by 0.0024, and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5->1.0 was flat to 6e-6, so LR magnitude and schedule shape are both at their optimum already; depth and width do not stack (depth 10 x dim 640 = 0.987079, worse than either alone, replicated three times in this cell); and width turns over just past 768 (my depth 7 @ dim 896 = 0.991800). I also measured that prepare.make_dataloader costs ~145ms per 262144-token batch of pure-Python packing against a ~162ms step, so throughput is capped near 1.8M tok/s and a prefetch thread cannot help (GIL-bound). What I would try next: the size grid is exhausted at depth 8 x dim 768 x batch 2^18 (0.981817 on the board), so the remaining headroom is not in shape or in the optimizer schedule -- I would attack the fp32 logits tensor (B*T*vocab, ~34GB and the dominant memory term, computed then discarded every step) with a chunked cross-entropy, which would free enough VRAM to test dim 768 at larger depth without the DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 penalty that confounded every wide run in this cell.
